source.check: returned unopposed: declared elected at the close of nominations, the only nomination for the division (Strabane Chronicle, 22 April 1933, p. 1, block images read: 'There will be only one contest, namely, in the Lislea division')

note: Triennial rural district council election. Voting in Tyrone took place on Wednesday 31 May 1933. The Lislea division was the only contested rural district division in the Strabane union; the rest were filled at the nominations (Strabane Chronicle, 22 April 1933, p. 1: 23 members declared elected; no nominations for Birnaghs, Camus, Clady and Killyclooney, whose retiring members were deemed elected). Birnaghs, Camus and Killyclooney are recorded from the 1930 return with the new council's first meetings (every member of the old board returned; each sits in June 1933). Clady received no nomination, so its retiring member, Mr. Joseph Mills, was deemed re-elected (Strabane Chronicle, 22 April 1933, p. 1); he then wrote declining to accept the councillorship ('When I didn't fill in any paper it was proof that I am done with them'), and the Council declared a vacancy on 13 June 1933 (Strabane Chronicle, 17 June 1933, p. 1, read on the page image); in November 1933 it appointed Mr. Thos. Stewart to fill the vacancy (Strabane Chronicle, 18 November 1933, p. 1), a co-option, not an election. Filed on 1933-05-31, the polling day for county council and rural district elections in Co. Tyrone that year (confirmed). Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Corrected from the page image of Strabane Chronicle, 17 June 1933, p. 1 (council-audit, Nov 2026): the round note said Clady 'is not recorded'; it now says Joseph Mills was deemed re-elected for Clady and then declined office. Renamed from 'Ballyfatton' to Ballyfatten (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1925-69 name the DED Ballyfatten; the rounds were filed as Ballyfatten (1924); Ballyfatton (1927, 1930, 1933, 1936, 1939, 1946, 1949, 1952, 1955, 1958, 1961, 1964, 1967). This round was filed as 'Ballyfatton', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (ballyfatton) answers with a redirect to this one.
